title: Consequences of PNU 282987 treatment in GCs exposed to 1% O2 for 24 h
projectDescription: Previous studies suggested a role of acetylcholine (ACh) in the regulation of the ovary. A target receptor, alpha 7 nicotinic ACh receptor (CHRNA7; encoded by CHRNA7), is expressed in the human ovary, e.g. by stromal cells, oocytes and human granulosa cells (GCs). The objective of this study was to explore its functions in cultured, in vitro fertilization (IVF)-derived GCs. For this, GCs exposed to 1% O2 were treated with the selective CHRNA7-agonist PNU 282987 for 24 h.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells were lyzed in 8 M of urea/50 mM NH4HCO3, sonicated for 15 min by Bandelin Sonoplus HD3200 cup resonator (Bandelin, Berlin, Germany) and centrifuged through QIAshredder devices (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) for 3 min (10°C, 2500×g). Protein concentration was determined using the Pierce 660 nm assay (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). For tryptic digestion, proteins were reduced with dithiothreitol (5 mM final concentration, 30 min at 56°C) and carbamidomethylated with iodoacetamide (15 mM final concentration, 15 min in the dark). Protein digestion was performed using the following three steps: (i) 4 h at 37°C, lysyl-endopeptidase C (Lys C; Fujifilm Wako, Neuss, Germany) 1:100 enzyme/protein ratio, (ii) dilution to 1 M urea with 50 mM NH4HCO3, (iii) overnight digestion at 37°C with modified porcine trypsin (Promega, Madison, WI, USA) in a 1:50 enzyme/protein ratio. For LC-MS/MS analysis peptides aliquots were injected on a nanoElute 2 chromatography system (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) and transferred with solvent A (0.1% formic acid in water) to a trap column (PepMap Trap-Cartridge, 300 μm × 5 mm, 5 μm particles, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). Peptides were separated on an Aurora Ultimate CSI 25×75 C18 UHPLC column (Ion Opticks, Collingwood, Australia) with the following steps: (i) gradient from 2% mobile phase of B phase (0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile) to 25% B in 25 min (ii) gradient from 25% B to 37% B in 5 min and (iii) gradient from 37% B to 95% B in 1 min and (iv) a 4 min equilibration step at 95% B. MS analysis was performed with a timsTOF HT mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) using a dia-PASEF method with the following parameters: (i) Mass range 475 – 1000 m/z, (ii) 1/k0 range of 0.85–1.27 (iii) number of MS/MS ramps 8, (iv) number of MS/MS windows 21, (v) estimated cycle time 0.95 sec.
dataProcessingProtocol: Collected spectra were analyzed using DIA-NN (V1.8) using predicted spectral libraries generated by the deep-learning-based spectra and retention time predictor. As input sequence database, the human subset of the UniProt database was used and a false discovery of 1% was applied for identification.
